script: This is the shape of AI writing. And this is the shape of human writing. Researchers figured out how to tell them apart without reading a single word, and they're right 93% of the time. So a team from Maryland and Google DeepMind ran 61,000 stories through a detector and found the giveaway had nothing to do with em dashes or the word delve. It was actually the structure of the story itself. So AI writing is too clean. It has no tangents, nothing unresolved, and it always spells out the outcome for you because it doesn't trust you to understand it. And get this, researchers found that AI over-explains themes 77% of the time, and every model does it differently. For example, Claude barely ever lets tension build, while GPT always reaches for gossip constantly, and Gemini always has this weird gravitational pull towards dark settings. So I took the full research paper, put it in Claude, and told it to read every finding as a rule it can never break while writing. Then I opened Skill Creator in the same chat, turned all of it into a permanent skill, and gave it a name called Human Scope. So now whenever I type slash human scope before any writing task, Claude already knows what human writing actually looks like and what to stop doing. The paper is called StoryScope. And if you want the link to read it, plus the Claude skill I made, comment SCOPE.
